ISIS Commander Killed In US-Nigeria Joint Military Operation—Trump
United States President Donald Trump has announced that American and Nigerian forces have killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, the second-in-command of ISIS globally, in a joint military operation conducted inside Nigeria.
Trump made the announcement late Friday in a post on his Truth Social platform, saying the mission was carried out at his direction.
“Tonight, at my direction, brave American forces and the Armed Forces of Nigeria flawlessly executed a meticulously planned and very complex mission to eliminate the most active terrorist in the world from the battlefield,” Trump wrote.
“Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, second in command of ISIS globally, thought he could hide in Africa, but little did he know we had sources who kept us informed on what he was doing. He will no longer terrorize the people of Africa, or help plan operations to target Americans,” Trump added.
Trump also thanked the Nigerian government for its cooperation in the mission, saying: “With his removal, ISIS’s global operation is greatly diminished.”
Al-Minuki, also identified as Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Mainuki, was considered one of the top-ranking figures within the ISIS leadership structure and allegedly functioned as the organisation’s global deputy commander.
He was sanctioned by the U.S. Department of State in 2023 under Executive Order 13224, which targets individuals and organisations linked to terrorism financing and activities.
According to the Counter Extremism Project, al-Mainuki primarily operated across the Sahel region in Africa, spanning nearly 12 countries.
He served as a senior commander of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and oversaw operations connected to the Lake Chad division under ISIS’s General Directorate of Provinces.
The operation comes after the U.S. struck what it said were Islamist bases in northwestern Nigeria on Christmas Day last year, following Trump’s accusations that Christians in Nigeria were being persecuted, which the Government denied.
Following those Christmas strikes, the U.S. reportedly sent small teams of troops to Nigeria on multiple occasions in pursuit of ISIS targets.
The Pentagon and Nigerian military authorities had not issued detailed independent confirmations as of Saturday morning.
The operation is being described as a significant blow to ISIS’s global leadership structure.

The United States has announced a significant victory in the global campaign against terrorism with the elimination of Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, the second-highest-ranking leader within the ISIS hierarchy. The operation, which took place in Nigeria, was confirmed by US President Donald Trump. According to the President, the mission was a highly coordinated and secretive effort conducted jointly by the United States military and the Nigerian armed forces. Trump shared the details of this successful strike on his social media platform, Truth Social, emphasizing that the operation was carried out under his direct orders to neutralize a high-value target who posed a severe threat to international security.
Details of the Secret Operation
President Trump described the mission as an extremely difficult and high-stakes operation that required precise intelligence and easy cooperation between the two nations. He noted that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki had been hiding in the vast landscapes of Africa, under the impression that he was beyond the reach of international justice, while however, US intelligence agencies had been meticulously tracking his every move, ensuring that the window of opportunity for the strike was perfectly timed. Who was Abu-Bilal al-Minuki?
Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, also known by the alias Abu Bakr ibn Mohammed ibn Ali al-Manuki, was recognized globally as the second-in-command of the Islamic State. He was a pivotal figure in the organization's expansion across the African continent, particularly within the Sahel region, while the Sahel is a massive geographical belt stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea, serving as a transition zone between the Sahara Desert to the north and the more fertile regions of sub-Saharan Africa to the south. This region encompasses several countries, including Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, Chad, and Sudan. Al-Minuki utilized this difficult terrain to coordinate terror activities and evade capture for an extended period.
Role in ISWAP and Global Terror Network
Reports indicate that al-Minuki served as a top commander for the Islamic State West Africa Province, commonly known as ISWAP. His influence was particularly strong in the Lake Chad region, where he oversaw numerous insurgent operations. Beyond direct combat, he was a key logistical mastermind responsible for the distribution of funds, weapons, and strategic instructions to various affiliated terror cells across the continent. His ability to manage the flow of resources made him an indispensable asset to the ISIS global network, and his death is viewed as a crippling blow to the group's operational capacity in West Africa.
A Long-Standing Target for the US
The United States had identified al-Minuki as a primary threat long before the recent operation. In June 2023, the US Department of State officially designated him as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT). This designation highlighted his status as one of the most dangerous individuals on the planet, triggering international sanctions and intensified efforts to locate him, while uS officials have reiterated that his death marks a turning point in the fight against the rising tide of extremism in Africa, where ISIS-linked groups have been increasingly active over the past few years. President Trump concluded his announcement by expressing his gratitude to the Nigerian government for their vital partnership in this mission, which has successfully dismantled a major pillar of the ISIS leadership structure.
